Issued at 240 PM EDT Tue Sep 15 2026

Today-tonight... Ridging aloft across the Deep South will remain in 
place today, with the axis stretching across the Florida peninsula. 
At the surface, high pressure expands along the eastern seaboard as 
a front draped over portions of the Deep South (and out into the 
western Atlantic) shifts southeast into north to north-central 
Florida this afternoon, and across central into tonight. Locally, 
the pressure gradient will begin to tighten this afternoon, 
resulting in the east-northeast winds increasing to 10-15 mph with 
gusts to around 20 mph. A diffuse east coast sea breeze has already 
formed this afternoon and is pushing inland. Deep moisture south of 
the aforementioned surface boundary will persist this afternoon, and 
will  aid in convection today, with forecast PW values of 2.0-2.2". 
Scattered showers and isolated storms formed late this morning along 
the sea breeze with activity increasing in coverage and intensity as 
the sea breeze pushes inland this afternoon. The greatest chance for 
showers and storms (PoP 50-60 percent) will be across the interior 
this afternoon as the sea breeze continues to push inland. Any 
lingering activity across the interior will diminish into early 
evening, with isolated to scattered showers and storms remaining 
possible along the coast in the onshore flow. 

The environment supports convection today with plenty of instability 
(MUCAPE 1900-2200 J/kg), sufficient shear (25-33 KT of shear from 
SFC-8km), adequate buoyancy (lifted index of -3 to -5), and decent 
downdraft potential (450-630 J/kg). However, poor lapse rates should 
generally limit organized stronger storms this afternoon. Because of 
this, main storm hazards today will be frequent lightning, gusty 
winds of 40-50 mph, and locally heavy rainfall. Due to warmer 
temperatures aloft (-5.5 to -6C at 500 mb), hail is not expected 
today. Outside of storms, temperatures are forecast to be 
seasonable, with afternoon highs in the upper 80s to low 90s. These 
temperatures combined with high humidity will produce peak heat 
indices of 100-107F. Warm and muggy conditions will continue 
tonight, with overnight lows in the mid to upper 70s, remaining 
warmest along the coast. 

Wednesday-Thursday... Upper level high pressure across the Deep 
South will move ever so slightly to the east on Wednesday and then 
remain in place through Thursday, with shortwave energy traversing 
across Florida through the period. An upper level trough will 
develop offshore the east coast of Florida on Thursday and slowly 
shift westwards towards the Florida peninsula through the day. At the 
surface,  high pressure along the eastern seaboard of the US will 
slowly shift eastward and offshore by late Thursday, while the axis 
remains over the Florida peninsula. Locally, the pressure gradient 
will continue to tighten on Wednesday, increasing the east to 
northeast flow to around 15-20 mph with peak gusts 25-30 mph at 
times. Conditions will remain breezy on Thursday, as east-northeast 
winds diminish to 10-15 mph with gusts to around 20 mph at times. A 
drier airmass will filter across north-central Florida on Wednesday, 
with a tight moisture gradient forecast across south-central 
Florida. The rain chances reflect this, with a low to medium (20-40 
percent) chance of rain from Orlando Metro to Cape Canaveral 
northward (where the driest air is forecast), and medium to high (50-
70 percent) chance of rain southward, with a few storms throughout 
the day. Rain chances on Thursday will be similar to Wednesday as 
the trough pushes a little closer to the Florida peninsula, with 
continued rounds of scattered to numerous showers and a few storms 
across the south with lower rain chances across the north, 
especially northwest of I-4. 

Temperatures will be seasonable, with afternoon highs in the upper 
80s to low 90s. Muggy and warm conditions will continue overnight 
and into early morning, with lows in the mid to upper 70s. However, 
areas along the Barrier Islands may struggle to fall below the 80 
degree mark each morning.

Due to the increase in winds on Wednesday, periods of poor to 
hazardous beach and boating conditions, a high risk of life 
threatening rip currents, and rough surf across all local beaches 
are forecast. The continued breezy conditions on Thursday will 
promote a high risk of rip currents continuing on Thursday. Heed 
the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags, and signs. Entering 
the surf is not advised!
